common.date-mask: Placeholder showing the expected date format. TRANSLATE THIS: the order of day, month and year differs by locale, so a French user should see jj/mm/aaaa and a German one tt.mm.jjjj. Keep the same number of characters per part.
common.dismiss: Dismiss button on a notification. A VERB, imperative. Slightly more formal than OK; both are used and both are translated once.
common.email-example: Placeholder in an email field. An EXAMPLE ADDRESS — translate the local part and the company word if that reads more naturally in the target language, and keep it a valid address.
common.ok: Dismiss button on a notification. An ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, and the shortest form the language allows. Used by every snackbar that offers one, so it is translated once.
common.page-number: Current page indicator with no known total. A NOUN plus a number.
common.page-of: Current page out of a known total. Both are numbers; word order may differ in the target language.
common.permission-denied: Shown when the server refuses an action for lack of permission. A STATEMENT about the user's rights, not an error in the system. Used across features, so it is translated once.
common.search-deleted: Confirms a saved search was removed. {{ name }} is the user's own content.
common.search-saved: Confirms a saved search was stored. {{ name }} is the name the user gave it, so it is their own content and never translated.
common.search-updated: Confirms a saved search was renamed or changed. {{ name }} is the user's own content.
common.select-item: Accessible name of the checkbox that selects one row in a document list. An IMPERATIVE instruction; `{{ name }}` is the document's own title and is NOT translated. Announced by a screen reader, never shown. Place the placeholder wherever the target language needs it.
common.tag-added: Confirms a tag was applied to a document. {{ name }} is the tag text, entered by a user.
common.tag-applied: Confirms a tag was applied from the document detail page. {{ name }} is the tag text.
confirm.add-a-permission: Title of the dialog that grants a permission on a saved search. A VERB phrase, imperative.
confirm.delete: Confirm button on a destructive dialog. A VERB, imperative, and the shortest form the target language allows — it sits next to Cancel. Used by every delete confirmation in the application, so it is translated once.
confirm.delete-collection: Title of the dialog confirming deletion of a collection. A collection groups documents; deleting it does not delete them.
confirm.delete-collection-question: Message of the collection-delete confirmation. A QUESTION.
confirm.delete-document: Title of the dialog confirming a soft delete of one document from its detail page.
confirm.delete-document-named: Message of the document soft-delete confirmation. {{ name }} is the DOCUMENT TITLE, repository content. A QUESTION seeking confirmation.
confirm.delete-document-question: Message of the soft-delete confirmation. A QUESTION seeking confirmation; keep it a question in the target language.
confirm.delete-group: Title of the dialog confirming deletion of a group, in administration.
confirm.delete-group-named: Message of the group-delete confirmation. {{ name }} is the GROUP NAME, server data, never translated. A QUESTION — keep the quotation marks the target language uses, and move the placeholder if word order requires it.
confirm.delete-saved-search: Title of the dialog confirming deletion of a saved search — a stored query, not any document.
confirm.delete-saved-search-named: Message of the saved-search delete confirmation. {{ name }} is the search the user named, so it is their own content and is never translated.
confirm.delete-selected-documents: Message of the BULK soft-delete dialog. {{ count }} is always 2 or more — the singular case uses confirm.delete-the-document instead, so this string never needs an "(s)" suffix and should read naturally as a plural.
confirm.delete-the-document: Message of the soft-delete dialog when the document has no usable title. A QUESTION. The definite article is deliberate: one specific document, unnamed here.
confirm.delete-user: Title of the dialog confirming deletion of a user account, in administration.
confirm.delete-user-named: Message of the user-delete confirmation. {{ name }} is the USERNAME, server data. Two sentences: a QUESTION then a WARNING; the second is the only place the user is told the action is irreversible.
confirm.delete-vocabulary-entry: Title of the dialog confirming deletion of one entry from a Nuxeo vocabulary (a controlled list of values).
confirm.delete-vocabulary-entry-named: Message of the vocabulary-entry delete confirmation. {{ name }} is the entry id and {{ directory }} the vocabulary name — both server data. Two placeholders, and their order may need to change in the target language.
confirm.got-it: Dismiss button on an informational dialog that asks for no decision. An ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, informal; not a confirmation of an action.
confirm.move-named-to-trash: Message of the soft-delete dialog when the document has a title. {{ name }} is the document name — keep the quotation marks the target language uses, and move the placeholder if word order requires it. A QUESTION.
confirm.move-to-trash: Title of the dialog confirming a SOFT delete. "Trash" is the recoverable area, so the wording must not imply permanence — contrast confirm.permanently-delete-document.
confirm.permanently-delete-document: Title of the dialog confirming an IRREVERSIBLE delete of one document. "Permanently" is the load-bearing word and must survive translation.
confirm.permanently-delete-documents: Title of the dialog confirming an IRREVERSIBLE delete of several documents. Plural.
confirm.permanently-delete-documents-cou: Message of the BULK irreversible-delete confirmation. {{ count }} is always 2 or more — the singular case uses confirm.permanently-delete-warning instead, so this should read naturally as a plural and never needs an "(s)" suffix.
confirm.permanently-delete-warning: Message of the irreversible-delete dialog. Two sentences: a QUESTION then a WARNING. Both matter — the second is the only place the user is told the action cannot be reversed.
confirm.update: Title of the dialog that edits an existing permission. A VERB, imperative.

login.panel-label: Accessible name on the main landmark wrapping the sign-in form. Same meaning as login.title; names the region for screen-reader users.
login.skip-link: Link at the top of the sign-in page that moves keyboard focus to the username field, bypassing decorative chrome. WCAG bypass-block link; a verb phrase.
login.title: Page heading on the sign-in screen. A verb phrase: authenticate to the application. Use the product's 'log in' wording consistently with nav.sign-out's 'sign out'.
nav.clipboard.copy: Button copying the clipboard's documents into the current folder. A VERB, imperative.
nav.clipboard.empty: Shown when the clipboard holds no items. The clipboard is an in-application staging area for copy/move, not the operating system clipboard.
nav.clipboard.hint: Instruction shown beneath nav.clipboard.empty. The quoted phrase "Add to Clipboard" is a menu item label the user will look for, so it must match the translation of that menu item exactly, and keep the quotation marks.
nav.clipboard.move: Button moving the clipboard's documents into the current folder. A VERB, imperative.
nav.clipboard.remove: Accessible name and tooltip on the button that takes one item out of the clipboard. A verb phrase.
nav.clipboard.tip: Guidance shown when the clipboard has items. 'Container' means a folder or other document that can hold children. 'Paste or move' are two distinct operations.
nav.collections.empty: Shown when the user has no collections. A 'collection' is a user-curated set of documents, a Nuxeo domain term.
nav.expired.empty: Shown when no documents have passed their expiry date. 'Expired' refers to a document retention/expiry date, not a session.
nav.favorites.empty: Shown when the user has marked no documents as favorites. 'Yet' implies the list can be filled, and is worth preserving.
nav.favorites.hint: Instruction shown beneath nav.favorites.empty explaining how to add one. 'Star icon' refers to a ★ button on each document row.
nav.favorites.remove: Accessible name and tooltip on the button that unmarks one document as a favorite. A verb phrase.
nav.folders.empty: Shown in place of the folder tree when the repository has no folders the user may see. Note it may mean 'none exist' or 'none visible to you'; prefer neutral phrasing.
nav.item.administration: Navigation entry for the admin area: users, groups, vocabularies, audit. A noun naming a section.
nav.item.assets: Navigation entry for digital assets - images, video, rich media. A noun, plural. Domain term: 'asset' here means a media file, not a financial asset.
nav.item.browse: Navigation entry for the folder tree and document list. A VERB, imperative - 'browse the repository', not the noun 'a browse'.
nav.item.browse-adf-hx: Navigation entry for the proof-of-concept browse page built on upstream components. ACRONYM: 'POC' means proof of concept. 'adf-hx' is a library name and MUST stay in English. Internal-facing; it will not ship to customers.
nav.item.clipboard: Navigation entry for the in-application staging area used for copy and move. NOT the operating system clipboard; if the target language distinguishes them, use the application sense.
nav.item.collections: Navigation entry for user-curated sets of documents. A noun, plural. Nuxeo domain term: a 'collection' is a named set a user assembles.
nav.item.dashboard: Navigation entry for the landing page of summary cards. A noun naming the page.
nav.item.expired-queue: Navigation entry listing documents past their retention expiry date. 'Expired' refers to a document retention date, not a session or a licence. 'Queue' is a worklist.
nav.item.favorites: Navigation entry for documents the user has starred. A noun, plural. US spelling in the source; use the target language's own convention.
nav.item.knowledge-discovery: Navigation entry for the AI-powered search over the repository. PRODUCT FEATURE NAME - 'Knowledge Discovery' names a Hyland capability and is normally kept in English; confirm with the translation crew before translating it. ACRONYM in the feature itself: AI means Artificial Intelligence.
nav.item.personal-space: Navigation entry for the user's own workspace folder. A noun phrase naming a place.
nav.item.recently-viewed: Navigation entry for the list of documents this user opened. An adjectival phrase describing the documents, not an instruction.
nav.item.search-filters: Navigation entry opening the saved-search and filter panel. 'Search' is a NOUN qualifying 'filters' - filters for searching, not an instruction to search for filters.
nav.item.settings: Top-level navigation item, and the accessible name of its drawer toggle. A NOUN naming the section.
nav.item.tasks: Navigation entry for workflow tasks awaiting this user. A noun, plural.
nav.item.trash: Navigation entry for deleted documents pending permanent removal. A noun naming a place, recoverable - not 'rubbish' or 'waste'.
nav.loading: Accessible name on a progress spinner, announced to screen readers while a navigation panel fetches data. A present participle describing an in-progress state.
nav.recent.empty: Shown when the user has not viewed any documents yet. 'Recently viewed' is a history of documents this user opened.
nav.refresh: Accessible name and tooltip on a small icon button that reloads one panel of the navigation drawer. A verb, imperative.
nav.sign-out: Button that ends the user's session. A verb, imperative. Note this is 'sign out', not 'log out' — keep the product's wording consistent with the sign-in screen.
nav.tasks.dashboard: Link to the full tasks page. 'Dashboard' is the name of that page. A verb phrase: 'view the tasks dashboard'.
nav.tasks.empty: Shown when the user has no workflow tasks awaiting action. 'Pending' means awaiting the user's action.
nav.tasks.retry: Button shown after the task list fails to load, which re-attempts the request. A verb, imperative.
nav.tree.retry: Button re-attempting a failed load of the personal space tree. A VERB, imperative.
nav.tree.root: Button returning the folder tree to the repository root. A NOUN.
nav.tree.toggle: Accessible name for the chevron button that expands or collapses one folder in the navigation tree. A VERB phrase, imperative. `{{ name }}` is the folder's own title and is NOT translated — place it wherever the target language needs it, which is the whole reason it is a parameter rather than appended to the end.
